advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish the empty-id harness message for the create-disposable path from the resolve-existing path so operators see which step failed.
evidence: 157: [ -n "$TICKET_ID" ] || harness "rebar ticket ${TICKET} did not resolve to a full canonical id"
In the else branch (lines 153-156) TICKET is empty, so the message reads 'rebar ticket  did not resolve...' which misdescribes a create failure.
advisory.finding: The disposable-ticket path emits a harness message that interpolates the empty ${TICKET}: line 157 fires when create_ticket returned an empty id, but reports 'rebar ticket  did not resolve to a full canonical id' with a blank id, obscuring that a disposable ticket was being CREATED (not resolved).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make ticket_id/create_ticket surface a non-zero exit (or a distinct sentinel) when rebar output is present but not a canonical id, rather than emitting empty-and-exit-0.
evidence: 143: tid = d.get("ticket_id") or d.get("id") or ""
144: print(tid if tid.count("-") == 3 else "")
154: TICKET_ID="$(create_ticket)" || harness "could not create disposable rebar ticket"

The python exits 0 and prints empty on any shape mismatch, so the `|| harness` guard is dead for that world; the check cannot distinguish 'create ran and produced nothing usable' from 'create never produced a valid id'.
advisory.finding: create_ticket / ticket_id fail OPEN on unexpected rebar output: the embedded python prints "" and exits 0 whenever the id lacks exactly 3 dashes, so `TICKET_ID="$(create_ticket)" || harness ...` (line 154) never triggers on a malformed-but-successful rebar response; only the separate emptiness check (line 157) catches it, and it cannot tell 'rebar failed' from 'rebar returned an id we rejected'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the removed negative-path mirror-lock assertion is fully owned/proven by S6 (infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md) so deleting it here leaves no coverage gap.
evidence: Diff removes the entire block guarded by 'gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/rulesets"' and the 'negative-path: direct push to GitHub main was REJECTED by the mirror-lock' pass line.
The removed block was the only in-script check of the out-of-band-push rejection guarantee; the header no longer mentions the negative path.
advisory.finding: The complementary NEGATIVE-PATH assertion (that a direct push / PR-merge to GitHub `main` is REJECTED by the gerrit-mirror-lock-main ruleset) was deleted from the script, removing a behavior this artifact previously proved opportunistically.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture and report ls-remote failure distinctly from a genuinely-absent mirror ref in the replication poll so a transient error is not reported as 'branch not visible'.
evidence: 183: gh_branch_sha="$(git ls-remote "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}" "refs/heads/${TEST_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
188: [ "${gh_branch_sha:-}" = "$GERRIT_BRANCH_SHA" ] || harness "test branch not visible on GitHub mirror: ${TEST_BRANCH}"
2>/dev/null discards ls-remote failure, so an empty result conflates 'network/auth error' with 'ref absent'; the harness verdict cannot name which occurred.
advisory.finding: The initial GitHub-mirror replication poll (lines 181-189) reuses the variable name `deadline` at top level and again inside poll_both_votes as a `local`; more importantly the loop relies on `gh_branch_sha` being set on the LAST iteration — if `git ls-remote` errors every iteration (2>/dev/null swallows it), `gh_branch_sha` stays empty and the harness at line 188 fires correctly, but a transient ls-remote failure on the final iteration before the deadline is indistinguishable from 'branch genuinely absent'.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-grep assertions in tests 1-3 with behavioral tests that drive the shell functions (or assert observable script outcomes) instead of matching implementation text.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_e2e.py:43 `assert 'git commit -q -s -m "test: reviewbot e2e probe ${stamp}${TRAILER}"' in text`
tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_e2e.py:69 `assert 'is_int "$llm" && [ "$llm" -lt "$LLM_REVIEW_MAX" ]' in text`
tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_e2e.py:67 `assert re.search(r'\\[ "\\$llm" != "NONE" \\] \\|\\| harness', text)`
The grepped target is the executable script infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh (the unit under test), not a non-executable instruction artifact, so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply.
Four-Criterion (a): renaming the local `llm`/`ver` shell vars or reflowing the commit-message line is behavior-preserving yet breaks these asserts.
blocking.finding: Three of the six new tests assert exact literal substrings of the shell script under test (reviewbot-e2e.sh) rather than its behavior; they are source-grepping change-detectors that break on any behavior-preserving refactor (renaming a local shell variable, reflowing a command) without detecting any behavior change.
scenarios: A maintainer renames a shell local or reformats a command; the tests fail despite identical behavior.
A real regression in vote-parsing or GATE-BLOCKED branching is introduced but the literal strings still match, so these tests stay green.
